# Sales Ops AI Toolkit

A real, tested Python toolkit combining the three technical asks from
Airbus Helicopters' "Werkstudent Sales Operations & AI Strategy" posting:
AI-powered capture planning, prompt engineering for sales outreach, and
lead-scoring / CRM data quality — built to close a gap for this specific
posting, since nothing in my existing project portfolio addressed the
sales domain.

## What this is (read before citing anywhere)

**The lead-scoring data is entirely synthetic**, generated by
`src/leads.py` — not real Airbus, helicopter-industry, or any other
company's CRM data. Feature-to-outcome relationships (budget confirmed,
engagement, prior customer, fleet size, etc.) are designed to be
realistic in direction but deliberately noisy, so the model has to learn
from genuinely imperfect signal rather than a disguised deterministic
rule.

**Capture-plan and outreach text generation is classical NLP (extractive
summarization + parameterized prompt templates), not a large language
model.** There is no Claude/Gemini/OpenAI API access in this environment.
Two things are built and disclosed separately:

1. `build_outreach_prompt()` generates the actual prompt text that would
   be sent to an LLM in production — this is the real prompt-engineering
   artifact the posting asks for, and it's inspectable and testable for
   structure and personalization even without a live model call.
2. `render_template_email()` is a deterministic template-fill fallback
   that produces a working, sendable-quality draft today, without
   needing any LLM at all. It is less fluent than what an LLM would
   generate from the prompt above — that's expected and disclosed, not
   hidden.

The capture-plan account summaries use **extractive summarization**
(frequency-scored sentence selection), not generative summarization —
every sentence in a summary is lifted verbatim from the input notes, so
nothing is fabricated, at the cost of being less fluent than an
LLM-generated summary would be.

If asked in an interview: I don't have real sales/CRM experience, I
haven't used enterprise capture-planning software, and the AI-generation
pieces here are classical ML/NLP, not an LLM-backed system, because I
don't have API access to one in this environment. This project
demonstrates the underlying skills the posting asks for — building a
scoring model on real (if imperfect) signal, evaluating it honestly,
designing reusable prompt templates, and assembling structured account
research — on a system I could actually build and verify myself.

## What this models

- **`src/leads.py`** — synthetic B2B sales-lead generator (900 leads by
  default) with realistic feature/outcome correlation plus injected
  noise and ~12% missing fleet-size data, mirroring an imperfectly
  maintained real CRM rather than a clean synthetic set.
- **`src/scoring.py`** — a lead-scoring classifier (scikit-learn
  logistic regression + one-hot encoding of categorical fields),
  evaluated with a genuine held-out train/test split. This is the
  posting's "Prozessoptimierung... Lead-Scoring" and "Datenpflege &
  Qualitätssicherung" tasks addressed directly.
- **`src/capture_plan.py`** — assembles a structured capture-plan
  document from account facts plus an extractive summary of free-text
  notes (e.g. public report excerpts) — the "AI-Powered Capture
  Planning" task.
- **`src/outreach.py`** — parameterized prompt templates for
  personalized outreach emails across three sales angles (cost
  displacement, greenfield capability, renewal/upsell), plus a
  deterministic no-LLM fallback — the "Prompt Engineering für Sales"
  task.
- **`src/pipeline.py`** — runs the full flow end-to-end: generates
  leads, trains and evaluates the scoring model, then produces a sample
  capture plan and outreach prompt/email for a realistic account.

## A note on the lead-scoring evaluation methodology

Having previously caught a memorization bug in an earlier project (a
ticket classifier that scored a suspicious 100% because of a bad
train/test split), this project's evaluation was built defensively from
the start: `train_and_evaluate()` uses `train_test_split` with
stratification on the actual row-level dataset (not a small finite
template pool), and a dedicated test
(`test_accuracy_is_not_suspiciously_perfect`) asserts accuracy stays
below 90% as a regression guard — if that test ever starts failing, it
means something is leaking the label into a feature, not that the model
"got better."

The real, current numbers (900 synthetic leads, 25% held-out test set,
seed 42): **65.3% accuracy** against a 42.7% positive-class base rate in
the test set (so a "predict majority class always" baseline would score
57.3%), **ROC-AUC 0.69**, precision 0.60, recall 0.56. This is a modest
but genuine lift over baseline — consistent with how noisy real sales
data actually is, not an inflated number.

## Verification

29 automated tests (`tests/test_sales_ops_toolkit.py`) covering: lead
generation determinism and realism (no degenerate all-0/all-1 labels,
missing data present), the scoring model's train/test split integrity,
the "not suspiciously perfect" regression guard, sane precision/recall/
ROC-AUC bounds, correct handling of unseen categorical values at
inference time, a directional sanity check (leads with strong positive
signal score higher than leads with weak signal), extractive-summary
correctness (summary sentences must come verbatim from the source text,
in original order), capture-plan field assembly, and outreach-prompt/
email personalization and input validation.

## Running it

```bash
pip install scikit-learn pandas
python3 src/pipeline.py          # generates leads, evaluates the scoring model, prints a sample capture plan + outreach prompt
python3 -m pytest tests/ -v      # runs all 29 tests
```
